title: Time-phased ML with regeneration biomarkers predicts post-hepatectomy liver failure
summary: The PILOT architecture used 55 perioperative variables, including GATA3, RAMP2, VEGFA and PEDF, to predict post-hepatectomy liver failure in 1,071 patients at three centers, with two external cohorts of 206 and 242. PILOT-Pre and PILOT-Intra used LightGBM and PILOT-Post used XGBoost, with AUCs of 0.740-0.895 in the validation cohorts, superior to traditional models (AUCs 0.502-0.644). The study is retrospective.
ai_technology: LightGBM and XGBoost models on time-phased perioperative data and liver regeneration biomarkers
organization: Tongji University; Second Military Medical University; Shanghai Tenth People's Hospital

evidence.tested: Thirteen algorithms were evaluated across preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative datasets with two external cohorts.
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation and clinical benefit are not shown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Gradient-boosted tree models integrated biomarkers and perioperative data to predict liver failure early.
